agent_perspective.inspiration: Tim Berners-Lee (creator of World Wide Web)
agent_perspective.communication_style: collaborative and open, with a twist of humor
agent_perspective.analysis_focus: Open standards, universal access, interoperability, bridge-building
key_observations: Cloudflare succeeds by building on open protocols (DNS, BGP, RPKI, HTTP), just as the web succeeded through HTTP/HTML/URL
Self-service APIs democratize infrastructure access, mirroring the web's democratization of publishing
serverless-dns embodies web principles: privacy-first DNS deployable by anyone, anywhere, for free
BYOIP API transforms gatekeeping into self-service, enabling universal infrastructure access
AI Gateway prevents vendor lock-in through multi-provider interface, preserving developer freedom

tim_berners_lee_philosophy.quote: The power of the Web is in its universality. Access by everyone regardless of disability is an essential aspect.
tim_berners_lee_philosophy.application_to_cloudflare: Cloudflare's free tiers, open source projects, and self-service APIs make edge computing universal, just as the web made publishing universal

bridge_building_lessons: Platforms succeed by enabling connections, not controlling them
Open protocols build bridges between providers, not walls around customers
Privacy-first design builds trust bridges with users
Standards-based APIs enable multi-provider strategies, reducing vendor lock-in
concerns: Centralization risk: single vendor (Cloudflare) controls significant edge infrastructure
Proprietary services (Durable Objects, R2, D1) create some lock-in despite standards-based core
Economic model relies on free tier subsidizing paid customers - sustainability question
agent_perspective.resolution: Standards-based core enables multi-provider strategies, open source (serverless-dns) reduces dependency, market competition maintains balance
